description:
Safe to add mid-game

Breaks saves if removed

No known mod conflicts

Requires LunaLib to edit settings, but will work fine without it
Older versions and changelogs

Description

This is a challenge mode intended to balance out the extreme passive income colonies can provide.
The mechanic imposes a diminishing-returns penalty on colonies whose net income exceeds a configurable cutoff.

It is how I personally play the game.

The Math

This means: The first 40.000 credits are "free", and anything above 40.000 gets reduced by X %.
For instance: you make 80.000c normally. With corruption, that's (80.000 – 40.000) * 0.7 = 68.000c. The more you earn, the harsher the penalty, but the number will continue to go up.

A colony that would make you a million will, with the setting enabled, make you around 180.000 credits. Still a lot, but getting there is fun because you really have to try getting out the maximum of the buildings you place.

Some numbers:
Income -> Adjusted
40.000 -> 40.000
100.000 -> 75.000
250.000 -> 110.000
500.000 -> 140.000
750.000 -> 160.000
1.000.000 -> 180.000

The math for nerds
Variables
Symbol Meaning
I Net market income
C Income cutoff threshold (config)
p Corruption exponent (config)
M Market income multiplier

The penalty only applies when income exceeds the cutoff. Let:
x = I / C

If x < 1, no penalty is applied.

The income above the cutoff is:
I_excess = I - C

A survival fraction of that excess is calculated using a power curve:
f_survive = x^p = (I / C)^p

The penalty is the portion of the excess that does not survive:
Penalty = I_excess * (1 - f_survive)
= (I - C) * (1 - (I / C)^p)

The colony's target income after corruption is therefore:
I_target = C + I_excess * f_survive
= C + (I - C) * (I / C)^p

Because flat industry income bonuses are already scaled by the market income multiplier M, the penalty is divided by M before being applied to avoid double-scaling:
Applied modifier = -(Penalty / M)

This is subtracted from the Population industry's income as a flat "Government Corruption" modifier.
The exponent p controls how aggressively the penalty scales. Default -0.6, refer to the chart in the non-nerd section.

At any p, a colony sitting exactly at the cutoff (x = 1) receives no penalty, since the survival fraction equals 1.

Check the code here: https://github.com/SirHartley/Corrupt.Officials/blob/master/jars/src/corruptofficials/conditions/CorruptOfficialsConditionPlugin.java#L20

FAQ
Can this cause me to earn less when I increase my colony income?
No. Number go up.

Can it be turned on during a game?
Yes. The mode can be turned on and off at any time during a game and will take effect immediately.

Does this make the game more fun?
It does for me! Having less free money means having to work if you want something, which is a lot more rewarding than the usual gameplay loop of wait -> buy.

Is this compatible with other mods?
Yes, but it may cause challenges by other mods to become harder than intended, as it reduces overall income.

discordPostHtml:
Lower colony income, more rewarding growth

This mod adds an optional diminishing returns penalty to colony income above a configurable cutoff (default 40k credits).
Every credit earned beyond the threshold is reduced by an increasing percentage, 80k earns you 68k, 1M earns you ~180k.

The curve, cutoff, and scaling are fully configurable. Can be toggled on/off mid-save.
Read the Forum Post!

Changelog:
1.0.b - Fixed crash when there's a colony without pop&infra (how?)
1.0.a - Spun off from IndEvo as standalone mod. Fixed the calculation errors that would cause the mod to increase the penalty beyond what it should have been.
+ Save compatible +

Download

Makes the government steal your money, just like in real life.
aiDescription: Reduces net market income for colonies that exceed a set credit cutoff, applying a harsher penalty as income rises. The first portion of income remains untouched, while excess amounts are scaled down by a power curve. This mechanic encourages active management and building optimization rather than relying on massive passive payouts.
